title: Ghost Ships: Crews That Vanished Without a Trace

scenes.text: December 1872. A ship drifts alone in the Atlantic, her sails still set to the wind.
There is no one at the wheel.
The Mary Celeste has been found completely abandoned.
Her cargo still sits untouched in the hold.
The crew's belongings are exactly where they left them.
A half-eaten meal waits on the captain's table.
The single lifeboat is gone, though the sea was calm.
Ten people vanished, and not one was ever found.
Fifty years later, the coast of North Carolina.
The Carroll A. Deering runs aground with every sail still raised.
Rescuers climb aboard and find the galley set for a meal.
The beds are made. The men's gear is packed and ready.
scenes.query: made bed dim room morning light

scenes.text: But the logbook, the anchors, and the entire crew are gone.
No storm. No wreckage. No bodies.
Locals call these waters the Graveyard of the Atlantic.
Then, 1947, the Strait of Malacca.
A distress call cuts through the radio static.
All officers are dead, it says. I am dying. Then nothing.
When help reaches the Ourang Medan, the deck is covered with the dead.
Every face is frozen, staring up at the sky.
There is not a single mark on any of them.
Before the ship can be towed, smoke pours from the hold.
The Ourang Medan explodes and sinks, taking its secret with it.
Some insist the ship never truly existed at all.
And still, the sea keeps collecting them.
Empty hulls. Silent decks. Meals no one came back to finish.
The water gives up the vessel, but never the crew.
To this day, no one can explain the ghost ships.
